name: Enterprise
scope: external KMS/HSM key descriptors and rotation bookkeeping
security_principles: SSO configuration does not itself grant agent authority
raw cryptographic key material is never represented in the enterprise layer
SAML metadata and SIEM endpoints require HTTPS
retention can be suspended by legal hold
organization-wide policies can constrain runtime behavior but cannot mint authority
compliance claims are generated from explicit evidence requirements

integration_strategy.sso: configuration/trust-binding contract; assertion verification delegated to hardened IdP/library
integration_strategy.retention: policy contract; deletion execution remains behind durable storage owners
integration_strategy.siem: redacted batch contract; actual delivery remains behind a controlled outbound adapter
integration_strategy.keys: KMS/HSM descriptor contract; no raw key bytes
integration_strategy.policy: organization-wide constraints evaluated in addition to Trust Kernel decisions

production_boundary_notes: The included in-memory key provider is a reference implementation only.
A production SAML implementation should use a hardened standards-compliant SAML library and enforce signature, audience, issuer, replay and clock checks.
A production SIEM sender should use the Phase 7 network egress boundary and a durable queue.
Retention enforcement should be executed by the owning durable stores and must honor legal hold.
